text:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV1 - serving runtime failures in eu-central-1. Symptoms: pod crashloops (exit 137), elevated 5xx rate, large variance in p95 latency. Paging @oncall-sam and @eng-runtime-lee.

oncall-sam: Oncall ack. Starting triage — joining voice. Grabbing cluster events and recent deploys.

eng-runtime-lee: Skimming pod logs: consistent pattern of CUDA allocation failures and then abrupt OOM kills: 
```
2026-03-15T09:10:12Z ERROR gpu_allocator.cc:45 Could not allocate 1.4GiB on device 0: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
container_linux.go:348: starting container process caused: process_linux.go:495: container init caused: "process killed"
```
Also seeing driver mismatch warnings on some nodes: 'nvidia-driver 525 != runtime 535' — possible mixed-driver fleet.

eng-platform-mat: Autoscaler events show a very fast ramp: nodes 30 -> 220 over 7m triggered by a burst from a single customer job + API retry storms. Immediately afterwards, the controller scaled down from 220 -> 40 in ~4m when queue drained. The rapid churn coincides with kubelet probe flaps and kube-proxy logs showing connection resets. Metrics: 
```
scale.up.rate: 26 nodes/min
scale.down.rate: 45 nodes/min
pod.restart.count: 132
```
This oscillation likely left GPUs in an inconsistent driver state and increased memory fragmentation.

eng-sre-rita: Quick mitigation suggestions: 
1) Pause burst autoscale and set min nodes to 60 for cluster inference pool.
2) Cordon/evict nodes showing driver mismatch and reboot them under controlled maintenance.
3) Flip traffic to quantized-fallback model group for high-memory models.
4) Apply temporary ingress rate-limit for the offending tenant(s).

oncall-sam: Executing step 1 & 3 now. Commands: 
```
rwctl autoscale pause --pool inference-eu-central
rwctl pool set --pool inference-eu-central --min-nodes 60 --max-nodes 120
rwctl rollout set --model-group high-mem --fallback quantized-v2
```
Applying ingress throttle for tenant 'analytics-big' at API gateway (50 rps).

customer-success-oliver: Pulling customer list: tenants impacted: analytics-big (heavy seq jobs), retail-sim (low but saw 40% errors), dev-playground (spike from tests). Notifying affected contacts: short comms sent.

eng-runtime-lee: Canary on quantized-fallback shows reduced memory use and far fewer container restarts. Error rate on canary nodes from 28% -> 4%. However, we need to evaluate quality for analytics-big workflows.

eng-platform-mat: Cordon + drain started on gpu-12 and gpu-17 which had mixed driver versions. Reboots scheduled; marking node qualification check to prevent rejoining if driver mismatched.

eng-sre-rita: Additional runtime tweaks pushed: lower default max_batch_size: 8 -> 3, set per-request kv-cache disabled for new sessions, bump probe initialDelaySeconds to 30 to avoid flapping during cold starts. Snippet: 
```yaml
runtime:
  max_batch_size: 3
  per_request_kv_cache: false
probes:
  readiness:
    initialDelaySeconds: 30
    periodSeconds: 10
```
Rolling this to 10% then up if stable.

oncall-sam: Observability: p95 latency falling, error rate reduced to ~6% cluster-wide after 12m. Keeping autoscale paused for 30m then gradual re-enable with cooldown.

deploy-bot: Deploy job 4972 detected a large batch job from tenant 'analytics-big' 4m before scale-up. Job triggered multiple retries due to transient errors.

eng-runtime-lee: Root cause hypothesis: a single tenant's long-context/batch workload plus an aggressive autoscaler policy caused a rapid node add. Many nodes came up with slightly different driver stacks (rolling image mismatch or node image skew), producing driver/ABI mismatch. The combination of driver state races and memory fragmentation triggered CUDA OOMs, causing container exits. The immediate scale-down then caused remaining pods to relocate rapidly, producing probe-induced restarts (brownout).

eng-platform-mat: Short-term actions (do now): 
- Keep autoscale paused and min=60 for 2h.
- Add 5m cooldown window and disable scale-to-zero for inference pools.
- Add driver-compatibility label check to node join hooks.
I'll file tickets for each.

customer-success-oliver: Customers acknowledged mitigations. One enterprise (analytics-big) requested ETA for full-resolution; responded with 2hr estimate for stabilization and follow-up RCA.

eng-sre-rita: Postmortem follow-ups: 
- Add autoscaler damping heuristics and per-tenant burst detection.
- Implement runtime memory guard: if estimated memory > 90% of node, reject batch with 429 and guidance.
- Add staging chaos test to simulate concurrent large-batch spikes.
- Harden node bootstrap to check GPU driver and runtime compatibility before marking Ready.

oncall-sam: Handoff: I'll continue monitoring for 90m. If stable, hand to @eng-sre-rita for day 2 follow-up + postmortem. Logging an incident timeline entry.

incident-bot: Incident created: incident/3912349999 - 'eu-central GPU OOMs + autoscale oscillation' - severity lowered to P2 at 3912352999 after mitigations. Postmortem owner: eng-sre-rita.

eng-runtime-lee: Planning to run a repro on staging: long-seq (8k tokens) + batch=6 to validate memory-guard thresholds. Will report results in ticket #INF-773.

eng-platform-mat: I'll push a small autoscaler config change to add scale cooldown and a per-tenant rate-breaker rule.

customer-success-oliver: Posting follow-up notes to customers and offering to help validate their jobs once we have a safe window. No requests for credits yet.

oncall-sam: Monitoring metrics: p50/p95 latency stabilized, 5xxs reduced to baseline. Keeping watch for 60m, will re-open pager if necessary. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Live pager closed; follow-ups queued in /incidents/postmortems/3912349999.
